title: liquid_glass_renderer: glass shapes demo
lede: A demo image from an open-source Flutter renderer for Liquid Glass: three clear glass shapes that bend a drawing grid at their rims.
summary: Three clear glass shapes refracting a grid. Open-source Flutter renderer, 2025.
made: 2025 (first pub.dev release June 13, 2025; image committed June 19, 2025)

evidence.note: Inspected the repository file packages/liquid_glass_renderer/doc/shapes.png (1844 × 1262) at commit c3209ea323. The stored copy is resized to 1600 px.

styles.note: An independent reimplementation that isolates the material: refraction at the rim and a specular edge, with no blur and no border.

context: pub.dev describes the package as “the raw renderer for a liquid glass effect in Flutter”. Its first version, 0.1.1-dev.0, was published on June 13, 2025, four days after WWDC. [pub.dev](https://pub.dev/packages/liquid_glass_renderer).

Wikipedia describes a wave of unofficial libraries after the announcement that approximate refraction and lensing with shaders, because platforms outside Apple have no native material. [Wikipedia: Liquid Glass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Glass).
observed: A beige-to-white gradient with a fine and a coarse grid of grey lines fills the frame.
Three glass shapes sit in a row: a rounded square, a circle, and a squircle with slightly flatter sides.
Inside each shape the grid lines stay straight in the middle but curve and compress in a band along the rim, as through a thick lens edge.
A thin bright highlight runs along the upper-left and lower-right rims. There is no fill color, no blur, no border, and no shadow.
interpretation: The image shows the one trait that separates the style from glassmorphism: the content under the glass is displaced, not blurred.
borrow: Test a glass effect over a regular grid. A grid shows at once whether the edge refracts or only blurs.

images.alt: Three clear glass shapes, a rounded square, a circle, and a squircle, on a beige grid. The grid lines curve near the edges of each shape.
